correctness.rationale: The two consecutive Caputo-Volterra identities differ by subtraction, so the earlier-time history integral must enter with a minus sign. The source instead prints a plus sign in equation (4.5). For constant forcing, exact integration gives the true increment proportional to \(((v+1)^h-v^h)\) and the printed increment proportional to \(((v+1)^h+v^h)\); at \(h=1,v=1,\Delta=1\) these are 1 and 3. An independent replay of the fixed-horizon printed recurrence for \(h=1,0.7,0.3\) shows growth proportional to \(1/\Delta\), while the exact terminal value is finite.
residual_risks: The claim diagnoses the printed derivation only; unavailable simulation code could have used a different corrected method.
